Fixed 99-negative HR@10 measures performance on that candidate protocol; sampled rankings can disagree with full-catalog rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Proposed inexpensive interval: cache each model’s per-user hit indicator; bootstrap 200 users with replacement independently within each category, preserving model pairing and candidate sets; compute Δ = ¼Σcategory mean(hit_new − hit_baseline). Use 10,000 replicates and report a prespecified 95% interval plus category deltas. Shared resampling indices preserve pairing ([SciPy documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). These intervals condition on four fixed datasets, trained models and sampled candidates; they exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty.

Repeated checkpoint and architecture selection can overfit finite validation data; bootstrapping the selected winner does not remove this bias ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Proposed protocol: prespecify ablations, GPU-second allocations, checkpoint evaluation times, stopping rules and one macro-HR@10 selection rule; count failed trials against the 43,200-second budget and retain every evaluated configuration. Treat validation intervals as exploratory after adaptive search; freeze the final choice before the host’s independent held-out evaluation.

History sensitivity alone does not establish useful sequence modelling: simple transition models already incorporate recency ([Spotify Research](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling)). Proposed test: prespecify popularity, last-item transition and recency-weighted item-to-item baselines; compare identical candidates. Measure truncation and older-history shuffling while preserving the last item. Fix the diagnostic-to-ablation prediction before evaluation, then assess whether sensitivity predicts paired gains over these baselines across planned configurations, controlling for category. Four category averages alone provide weak evidence; perturbation sensitivity without predictive gains remains descriptive.
